title: DC Has Officially Killed Off The One Hero Stan Lee Wished He Created
summary: DC ends its greatest anti-hero's immortality, sending off the one character Stan Lee wished Marvel created first with a proper farewell.
content: Forty-three years after DC beat Stan Lee to the creation of a unique comic book character, Marvel's rival company finally kills the immortal anti-hero. Since their beginnings, Marvel popularized numerous breakthrough characters that DC later echoed. Namor the Sub-Mariner debuted two full years before Aquaman , and the Human Torch beat Firestorm to the punch by decades, while Man-Thing preceded Swamp Thing by mere months in 1971. Likewise, Marvel turned Spider-Man into a relatable teenage hero years before DC introduced Static and Sideways, made Iron Man a billionaire armored icon before Steel, and later inspired DC's the Terrifics with Fantastic Four.

title: Forget Ted Lasso, TV's Best Sports Drama Still Hasn't Been Topped
summary: Ted Lasso brought sports dramas back to the forefront of the television landscape, but it's actually not the best the genre has to offer.
content: When it premiered in 2020, Ted Lasso immediately endeared itself to audiences with its heartwarming tone and lovable characters. Over four seasons, the show has celebrated soccer, but also championed a message that extends far beyond the sport itself. More than anything, Ted Lasso is a passionate endorsement of tight-knit community, healthy masculinity, and embracing your emotions.

title: Netflix Discloses Just How Much Streaming Relied On Book Adaptations In 2025
summary: Netflix's strategy of adapting books into hit series has become an industry standard, but has a massive impact on streaming viewership in recent news.
content: Page-to-screen adaptation is hardly a new phenomenon, but over the course of the last decade, platforms like Netflix have perfected the art, and the streamer has even shared just how heavily they've relied on adapting books in recent years. While many readers know just how important the publishing industry has been to keeping the entertainment industry moving forward with new characters and stories through the years, the resurgence of the high-quality page-to-screen adaptation has taken on a whole new life in the streaming era. With shows like Bridgerton and The Lincoln Lawyer captivating audiences, Netflix has made their relationship with books a public affair.

title: 12 Worst TV Remakes Of All Time
summary: From an unmysterious remake of The Prisoner to a painfully unfunny remake of The Inbetweeners, these are the worst TV remakes of all time.
content: Hollywood can’t resist plundering familiar I.P. for an easy buck. There’s currently a Cheers remake in the works for UK audiences . That same team could’ve just made an original sitcom about the staff and regulars of a pub, but Cheers is a brand name that brings a built-in audience. Television is one of the last bastions of original storytelling — something like Severance or Yellowjackets or The Bear would be too risky for movie theaters, but TV execs are willing to take those risks — but it’s also home to a thousand Marvel shows and Star Wars shows and Yellowstone spinoffs.
